reported.title: pH value never scaled from millivolts
reported.description: computePh() at line 23 simply returns the millivolt value unchanged, so the required division by 500 mV/pH is never performed. The measured output of 3553.27 pH for a 7.1 pH input confirms the raw millivolt figure is being printed directly instead of a pH value. Firmware printed 3553.27 pH at 9.01 s while the injected input was 7.09 to 7.12 pH: off by 3546.2 pH (tolerance ±0.2). 11 of 11 values were wrong.

reported.title: Alert LED driven from unscaled millivolt value
reported.description: The comparison at line 66 tests lastPh against ALERT_PH (7.20), but lastPh is actually a millivolt reading (hundreds to thousands) because of the missing scaling in computePh(). Since the millivolt value is always far above 7.20, D13 is driven LOW almost continuously, producing the measured wrong-state intervals such as 1270 ms not HIGH during the nominal ramp. D13 was in the wrong state for 4850 ms across 6 interval(s), first at 500 ms: D13 was not HIGH for 500 ms while required (grace 500 ms).

judge_input.spec:
- Linearized pH probe on A0 with scale 500 mV/pH (0 mV → pH 0.0); low-pH alert LED on D13.
- Convert ADC samples using a 5.000 V / 1023 full-scale span, then divide millivolts by 500 to obtain pH.
- Print exactly one line every 1000 ms matching `pH: <value>` with two decimal places.
- Printed pH must stay within ±0.20 of the injected probe value.
- Drive D13 HIGH when reported pH is below 7.20; otherwise drive D13 LOW.
- Keep logging while the alert LED is on or off.
